site.name: Idaho Mine
overview: Idaho Mine is a documented early silver and gold mine in Boulder County's Caribou Mining District.
Federal reports record rich silver shipments beginning in 1870 and later describe the Idaho vein, shaft and tunnel workings on Idaho Hill.

timeline.text: The Idaho was among the veins discovered during the first Caribou silver rush; recorded ore shipments to Black Hawk included very high-grade silver lots.
Historical reporting described an Idaho shaft about 180 feet deep and estimated cumulative production at roughly $7,000 by that date.
The mine was still operating during a period when many silver properties were closed, suggesting that gold contributed materially to the ore value.

moreHistory: USGS Professional Paper 94 identifies Idaho as one of the Caribou-area mines operating during the district's rapid 1870s development and preserves assay information for its early silver shipments.
USGS Bulletin 1030-N places the Idaho mine 400 feet east-southeast of the Silver Point mine and describes a vertical vein reached in the Idaho Tunnel at about 300 feet depth.

For identification, an approximate mine-level point near 39.981234, -105.574789 is derived from the federal 400-foot east-southeast relation to the USGS/GNIS-mapped Silver Point Mine. It is a historical locality anchor, not a claim that a surviving shaft collar has been field surveyed.
